title: Vision
content:
To keep infrastructure legible. The goal is a platform where a new engineer can read the repository, predict what a merge will do, and trust the result in production without a runbook.
Three commitments follow from that, and they are the standard we hold our own work to:
Reproducible over assembled. Everything a system needs should exist in version control and be produced by a command. If it was typed by hand at 2 a.m., it is a defect waiting for a holiday. Observable over assumed. If a change cannot be seen in metrics, logs, and traces before it ships, it is not finished. A silent failure costs more than a noisy one. Portable by construction. Cloud-agnostic design is what stops a vendor decision, a price change, or a regional outage from becoming an incident.
We expect AI to change how the work is done rather than what the work is. The judgement calls, the failure modes, and the operating discipline stay with the engineers who own the system.
